Plasma Glucose Range Required for Admission/Dosing
data.description: Admission may be rescheduled if plasma glucose is outside the required range on Day 1
data.text: Admission can be rescheduled if PG level is not 90 to 250 mg/dL on Day 1.

data.name: Hypoglycemia Induction Target (Insulin Infusion Stop Criterion)
data.description: Insulin infusion stop trigger and prerequisite for study treatment administration
data.text: Insulin infusion is stopped once bedside PG is <60 mg/dL; approximately 5 minutes later study drug is administered (Time = 0 min).

data.name: Edinburgh Scale Assessment During Hypoglycemia
data.description: Timepoint condition defined by plasma glucose level during hypoglycemia induction
data.text: During hypoglycemia induction will be when PG ≤75 mg/dL.

data.name: Insulin Regimen Acceptability
data.description: Review of insulin regimen prior to hypoglycemia induction procedure
data.text: Review patients' insulin regimens to confirm acceptability to undergo the procedure to induce hypoglycemia.

data.name: Interim Safety Review After First 6 Patients
data.description: Safety gating condition before remaining patients are dosed
data.text: Safety data will be reviewed after the first 6 patients (regardless of type of diabetes) are administered LY900018 in Period 2, and the remaining patients will be dosed after confirmation of the safety. The investigator and Lilly CRP or scientist will review available safety data, including AEs, SAEs, vital signs, ECGs, and safety laboratory tests, from these patients after they complete Period 2 Day 1. If no clinically significant safety findings for treatment or study procedure are noted, the remaining patients will be dosed.

data.name: Insufficient Response to Glucagon
data.description: Protocol-defined procedures to follow if the patient has an insufficient response to glucagon administration
data.text: Procedures for Insufficient Response to Glucagon Administration (Section 9.2.4).

data.name: Discharge Criteria / Investigator Discretion
data.description: Conditions governing discharge from the CRU
data.text: Patient may be discharged 6 hours after glucagon administration. A patient may remain inpatient at the CRU at the discretion of the investigator. All patients will receive a carbohydrate-rich meal prior to discharge and the investigator will ensure the patient's PG is stable; a prandial insulin dose will be administered if needed.

data.name: TE ADA Additional Follow-up Condition
data.description: Condition triggering and ending additional immunogenicity follow-up
data.text: Patients with TE ADA at follow-up/ED will undergo additional follow-up; samples for immunogenicity should be collected every 12 weeks (84±7 days) until the titer returns to baseline (ie, returns to within a single 2-fold dilution of the baseline titer) or until 1 year after the last dose of study treatment.

data.name: Fasting Condition for Laboratory Samples
data.description: Fasting requirement differs between screening/follow-up and treatment periods
data.text: Patients do not need to fast for samples at screening or follow-up. At Periods 1 and 2, samples should be collected from patients who have fasted at least 8 hours before any study procedures.

data.name: Non-inferiority Decision Criterion
data.description: Primary analysis success condition
data.text: Non-inferiority of LY900018 will be declared if the upper limit of the 2-sided 95% CI constructed on the difference in percentage (IMG - LY900018) is less than the NIM of 10%.

data.name: Patient Replacement Condition
data.description: Condition under which discontinued patients may be replaced
data.text: If patients discontinue from the study before completion of both periods with evaluable primary outcome for any reason, the patient may be replaced. Replacement should not occur beyond 75 patients enrolled, if it is expected to have at least 66 patients complete the study.

data.name: Postmenopausal Status Confirmation
data.description: FSH testing performed only when needed
data.text: FSH (female patients only) performed when needed to confirm postmenopausal status.

data.name: Inadvertently Enrolled Patient Continuation
data.description: Condition allowing an inadvertently enrolled patient to remain in the study
data.text: If the sponsor or investigator identifies a patient who did not meet enrollment criteria and was inadvertently enrolled, a discussion must occur between the Lilly CP/CRP and the investigator to determine if the patient may continue in the study. If both agree it is medically appropriate to continue, the investigator must obtain documented approval from the Lilly CP/CRP.

data.name: Screening to Period 1 (Randomization) Transition
data.text: Patients will undergo a screening examination within 28 days prior to enrollment. Prior to study drug administration on Period 1 Day 1, patients will be randomly assigned to a treatment sequence (either LY900018 in Period 1 and IMG in Period 2, or vice versa).

data.name: Admission/Dosing Gate on Plasma Glucose
data.text: Admission can be rescheduled if PG level is not 90 to 250 mg/dL on Day 1.

data.name: Period 1 to Washout Transition
data.text: Patients will be administered a single dose in Periods 1 and 2, which will be separated by a washout period of 3 to 14 days.

data.name: Washout to Period 2 (Crossover) Transition
data.text: After a washout of 3 to 14 days, patients cross over to the alternate treatment in Period 2; procedures in Period 2 will occur at approximately the same time as those in Period 1.

data.name: Period 2 to Follow-up Transition
data.text: Patients will return for a follow-up visit 26 to 30 days (within 28±2 days) after the last study treatment.

data.name: Follow-up to Additional TE ADA Follow-up Transition
data.text: Patients with TE ADA at follow-up/ED will undergo additional follow-up with immunogenicity samples every 12 weeks (84±7 days) until titer returns to baseline or until 1 year after the last dose.

data.name: Dosing Hold Pending Interim Safety Review
data.text: Safety data will be reviewed after the first 6 patients are administered LY900018 in Period 2; the remaining patients will be dosed only after confirmation of safety (no clinically significant safety findings).

data.name: Rescue for Insufficient Glucagon Response
data.text: Procedures for insufficient response to glucagon administration will be followed (Section 9.2.4); after completion of all PK sampling patients will be provided a carbohydrate-rich meal and a prandial insulin dose will be administered if needed to ensure PG stability.

data.name: Discontinuation from Study - Other Research Enrollment
data.text: Enrollment in any other clinical study involving an investigational product or enrollment in any other type of medical research judged not to be scientifically or medically compatible with this study.

data.name: Discontinuation for Medical, Safety, or Regulatory Reasons
data.text: Participation in the study needs to be stopped for medical, safety, regulatory, or other reasons consistent with applicable laws, regulations, and good clinical practice.

data.name: Discontinuation by Investigator Decision
data.text: The investigator decides that the patient should be discontinued from the study for any reason. If this decision is made because of an AE, SAE, or a severe hypoglycemia event, appropriate measures are to be taken and Lilly or its designee is to be alerted.

data.name: Discontinuation by Patient Decision
data.text: The patient, or legal representative, requests to be withdrawn from the study.

data.name: Discontinuation of Inadvertently Enrolled Patients
data.text: A patient who did not meet enrollment criteria and was inadvertently enrolled may be discontinued unless the Lilly CP/CRP and investigator agree it is medically appropriate to continue, with documented sponsor approval, with or without continued treatment with investigational product.

data.name: Early Discontinuation (ED) Visit
data.description: Patients discontinuing from the study prematurely for any reason must complete AE and follow-up procedures as shown in the Schedule of Activities; the Follow-up/ED visit occurs within 28±2 days after last study treatment.

data.name: Study Completion
data.description: Completion of both treatment periods (Period 1 and Period 2) with evaluable primary outcome and the follow-up visit 26 to 30 days after the last study treatment; patients with TE ADA complete additional follow-up until titer returns to baseline or 1 year after last dose.

data.name: Termination of the Study for Safety
data.description: Following the review of the safety data from the first 6 patients to complete Period 2 Day 1, the study will be stopped if deemed necessary for patient safety in the opinion of the investigator and sponsor.

data.name: Lost to Follow-up
data.description: A patient will be considered lost to follow-up if he or she repeatedly fails to return for scheduled visits and is unable to be contacted by the study site, after diligent attempts at contact by site personnel.

data.name: Admission/Dosing Eligibility Decision
data.description: Decision on Day 1 of each period whether to proceed with hypoglycemia induction or reschedule admission based on PG 90 to 250 mg/dL, insulin regimen review, and fasting status.

data.name: Insulin Infusion Stop and Study Treatment Administration Decision
data.description: Once bedside PG reaches <60 mg/dL, insulin infusion is stopped and approximately 5 minutes later study drug is administered (Time = 0 min).

data.name: Interim Safety Review Decision (First 6 Patients)
data.description: After the first 6 patients complete Period 2 Day 1, the investigator and Lilly CRP/scientist decide whether to dose the remaining patients or stop the study.

data.name: Discharge Decision
data.description: Decision at 6 hours post glucagon administration whether to discharge the patient or keep the patient inpatient at the investigator's discretion.

data.name: TE ADA Additional Follow-up Decision
data.description: At Follow-up/ED, determine whether treatment-emergent antidrug antibodies are present requiring additional follow-up every 84±7 days.

data.name: Insufficient Glucagon Response Decision
data.description: Assessment of response to glucagon administration and initiation of rescue procedures if the response is insufficient.

data.name: Primary Non-inferiority Analysis Decision
data.description: Final analysis decision based on the upper limit of the 2-sided 95% CI for the difference in treatment success percentages versus the 10% non-inferiority margin.
